name: Battery
label: Revelation
lede: A D.C. straight edge band that was bigger in Germany than at home, broke up six months after its Revelation album, and came back twenty years later with a song about its singer's teenage years in a mental hospital.

eras.title: First called Fury
eras.text: Battery started in Washington in 1990 as Fury, a youth crew band in the city that invented straight edge. It nearly ended as soon as it began, then a German label gave it a second life.

years.h: Fury becomes Battery in Washington, D.C.
years.p: [[Brian McTernan|eda2cb2f-b2c6-4e74-9fd7-49ea52df4172]] sings, with [[Ken Olden|94959ed9-83ae-46e1-b23f-88939fad93e6]] and Matt Squire on guitars, Toshi Yano on bass and Zac Eller on drums. The band starts out as Fury.

years.h: Brian McTernan's life falls apart after Battery's first show
years.p: According to a RevHQ interview, soon after the first show McTernan's life came apart: depression, fights, and a hospital stay. The band stalled; Olden and Eller started Worlds Collide, McTernan started Ashes.
The debut 7" on Deadlock Records, with Brian McTernan, Ken Olden, Matt Squire, Toshi Yano and Zac Eller.

years.h: We Won't Fall: Germany's Lost & Found revives Battery
years.p: Germany's Lost & Found Records puts out re-recorded versions of the 7" songs. It sells well enough that Battery re-forms to record and tour Europe.

eras.title: Big in Europe
eras.text: At home Battery were a D.C.-area band. In Europe, where Lost & Found pressed their records, they were a draw, and those tours gave Brian McTernan the confidence he'd later bring to the studio.

years.h: Only the Diehard Remain, Battery's first album
years.p: Out on Tidal and Lost & Found: sing-along youth crew hardcore with, in Revelation's words, very sincere lyrics.

years.h: Battery tour Europe, where they're bigger than at home
years.p: Battery tour North America and Europe through the mid-'90s. Wikipedia notes they were known mostly around D.C. in the US while doing well in Europe; McTernan credits those tours with his confidence.

years.h: Until the End and a new drummer from [[Frodus|ea524f94-2e37-414d-a7e9-61ba96472f0a]]
years.p: The second album comes out on Conversion and Lost & Found. [[Jason Hamacher|00a29c28-a1f0-4590-8055-6a94f407f19b]], also drumming in Frodus, joins in 1996.

years.h: Ken Olden and Ray Cappo make [[Better Than a Thousand|9a5d50be-8dff-4f2f-8852-aa4eafb8f985]]
years.p: Olden's side project with Graham Land and [[Ray Cappo|e8357f9d-f7f5-4858-a766-aef004bb38a6]] of [[Youth of Today|9ca27db4-f127-4aeb-ae87-29e21f558c13]] releases Just One on Revelation (REV 060). Revelation says Cappo's voice audibly wears out by the end.
Twelve songs on Revelation, A review quoted on Revelation's site calls it Battery's strongest, with the production the one complaint.

years.h: Battery break up six months after Whatever It Takes
years.p: Battery end within six months of the Revelation release. McTernan moves on to [[Miltown|a833c30f-40e5-4b26-aaaa-906ed2d843fb]] and a producing career; Olden keeps playing in [[Damnation A.D.|52ae8d28-e8f6-4ac5-8653-c9ffcc0bfc0f]]

eras.title: The basement studio
eras.text: Brian McTernan had started recording bands at 18 in the basement of a shared house in Boston, and named the studio Salad Days after the Minor Threat song. After Battery it became his main job.

years.p: A discography compilation gathers Battery's recordings from the Fury days through 1997.

eras.title: The first song in twenty years
eras.text: A one-off reunion for Revelation's 25th anniversary turned into a string of festivals, then a new song, a charity compilation and a European tour.

years.h: Battery reunite for Revelation's 25th anniversary in New York
years.p: Battery play Revelation's 25th anniversary shows in New York City. Offers follow from Damaged City Fest in D.C. and from REVfest.

q: It felt great to write a Battery song after so many years
years.h: My Last Breath: Battery's first new song in 20 years
years.p: Brian McTernan's lyric faces his teenage years in a mental hospital and is dedicated to his daughter. It leads off Revelation's Battery collection For the Rejected by the Rejected.
years.xp:
The proceeds go to the Center for Infant and Child Loss in Baltimore. Drummer Jason Hamacher told WBGO that two friends of the band lost children in 2013, one during delivery and one to sudden infant death, and that shaped why Battery came back.

The song was recorded with Paul Leavitt. Battery toured Europe that fall.

years.h: Full set filmed by hate5six, April 7, 2017
yt: Full set filmed by hate5six, April 7, 2017

years.p: McTernan fronts a new band with members of [[Bane|adf5ac61-4d7b-4cbc-95ce-ee2dc486f884]] and [[Darkest Hour|e0ededb4-6085-4f68-90f7-89bc560930a3]].

eras.title: Back on Revelation, behind the desk
eras.text: McTernan's studio work kept him in the Revelation family long after Battery's last record.

years.h: Brian McTernan produces Calling Hours for Revelation
years.p: McTernan produces Say Less by [[Calling Hours|a76e3280-2524-461d-855f-0550ebedff93]], the band of [[Farside|c6d7e9ab-e369-4dc2-b6a8-1fa7def9c069]] singer Popeye Vogelsang, and helped steer it to Revelation.
